adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `destinationCalendar` from a single object to an array and updates Google’s `createEvent` calendar selection to `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`, falling back to `"primary"` when no match is found. For legacy destination calendars where `credentialId` is null/undefined, this `find` never matches, so Google inserts into `primary` instead of the selected destination `externalId` (previously it used `destinationCalendar.externalId` directly). Additionally, in `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, the no-`credentialId` branch calls `createEvent(c, event)` without passing the destination `externalId`, so `CalendarManager.createEvent` returns `externalId` undefined, and `EventManager` stores `externalCalendarId: result.externalId` as undefined. Later, Google `updateEvent`/`deleteEvent` compute the calendar id using `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`, which cannot recover a missing externalCalendarId, leading to updates/deletes targeting the wrong calendar (or primary) and likely failing. This is a verifiable regression exposed by the diff.
